# R2 Gal 2:15–3:14 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** 2529–3395
**Lines actually read:** 1–867 (slice L2529–L3395; full exclusive range)
**Claim count:** 52

## Claims

### C-R2-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, justification]
- **claim:** Moo treats Gal 2:15–21 as a transitional definition of “the truth of the gospel”: it looks back to Antioch and ahead to the Galatian argument, with v. 16 as the key assertion that justification is by faith in Christ, not works of the law.
- **quote:** “We may then view the paragraph 2:15–21 as a positive assertion of this truth of the gospel.”
- **locus:** L2539
- **passage:** Gal 2:15–21

### C-R2-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo notes that key theological vocabulary (νόμος, ἔργα νόμου, δικαιόω, δικαιοσύνη, πίστις/πιστεύω, ζάω) is concentrated in 2:15–21 and introduced for the rest of the letter, which most scholars still place as the close of 1:11–2:21 rather than the start of the central argument.
- **quote:** “in verses 15–21 Paul introduces some of the key theological themes that will dominate the rest of the letter”
- **locus:** L2557
- **passage:** Gal 2:15–21

### C-R2-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** For Moo, vv. 15–16 state the essential point: Jews like Paul and Peter know they are justified by faith in Christ, not works of the law; Paul sets an antithesis (Christ, therefore not law) against the agitators’ synthesis of faith and law.
- **quote:** “In place of the agitators’ synthesis of faith in Christ and the law, Paul insists on an antithesis: it is Christ and therefore not the law.”
- **locus:** L2559
- **passage:** Gal 2:15–16

### C-R2-004
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Moo’s preferred reading of 2:17–20: Jewish Christians seeking justification “in Christ” abandon the law and thus appear as “sinners” like Gentiles, but Christ is not a servant of sin; rebuilding the law as authority would make them true transgressors; Paul models dying to the law to live for God.
- **quote:** “What Jewish-Christians need to do is imitate Paul, who, in order truly to live for God, has replaced his attachment to the law with an attachment to Christ (vv. 19–20).”
- **locus:** L2559
- **passage:** Gal 2:17–20

### C-R2-005
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Moo reads v. 21 as arguing that seeking righteousness by the law denies the epochal, gracious effect of Christ’s death; the death of God’s Son relativizes every other means of righteousness.
- **quote:** “to seek righteousness by the law is actually to deny the effect of that death—in the epochal significance with which Paul views it.”
- **locus:** L2559
- **passage:** Gal 2:21

### C-R2-006
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Against readings that merge forensic justification into participatory transformation (Gorman; D. Campbell), Moo holds justification/righteousness in Galatians as forensic, while union with Christ is a (perhaps the) key idea; they are inseparable but distinct effects of union with Christ.
- **quote:** “The person who is joined to Christ enjoys both forensic justification (vv. 16, 21) and transformation (vv. 19–20). They are inseparable but distinct effects of our union with Christ.”
- **locus:** L2561
- **passage:** Gal 2:16–21

### C-R2-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, new-perspective-on-paul]
- **claim:** Moo insists that despite salvation-historical emphases in current scholarship, the letter’s central argument is framed by principial statements about justification by faith for Jews and Gentiles (2:16; 5:4–5).
- **quote:** “the central argument of the letter is framed by principial statements about justification by faith—applied to both Jews and Gentiles (2:16; 5:4–5).”
- **locus:** L2563
- **passage:** Gal 2:16; 5:4–5

### C-R2-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 2:15, Moo takes “we Jews by birth” as continuing the Antioch speech content (mildly concessive toward v. 16): even privileged Jews turn from Moses’ law to faith in Christ; “sinners from among the Gentiles” is traditional Jewish language Paul uses only to spring the trap that all need justification in Christ.
- **quote:** “The gospel reveals that all people are “sinners” and therefore equally in need of finding justification in Christ.”
- **locus:** L2569
- **passage:** Gal 2:15

### C-R2-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, works-of-the-law, new-perspective-on-paul]
- **claim:** Moo’s core claim on 2:16: the dispute was not whether Christ-faith is needed for justification, but whether works of the law must be added; Paul’s real force is that Jews, not only Gentiles, are “sinners” whose covenant obedience cannot put them right with God.
- **quote:** “He is not arguing that Gentiles should be included, with Jews, in the people of God; he is arguing, rather, that Jews should be included, with Gentiles, in the mass of ordinary humanity.”
- **locus:** L2571
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-010
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, covenantal-nomism, new-perspective-on-paul]
- **claim:** Moo defines ἔργα νόμου as “doing what the law requires” (likely objective genitive: works done in obedience to the law), agreeing with Dunn’s late formulation of the phrase’s denotation.
- **quote:** “The phrase ‘works of the law’ simply denotes doing what the law requires.”
- **locus:** L2577
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-011
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, covenantal-nomism, new-perspective-on-paul, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** Moo summarizes the New Perspective: works of the law mark Jewish covenant identity (esp. circumcision, food, festivals) under covenantal nomism; they cannot justify because Messiah has come and Gentiles are no longer to be excluded—salvation-historical, not classic “legalism.”
- **quote:** “Why, then, can’t “works of the law” justify? Because they are torah works: insisting on them is effectively to turn back the clock in salvation history”
- **locus:** L2579
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-012
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, covenantal-nomism, new-perspective-on-paul]
- **claim:** Moo grants that the agitators were “nomists” (faith + law for ultimate salvation), not legalists seeking salvation by works alone, and that Paul often abbreviates “works of the law” as “law,” not “works.”
- **quote:** “they were “nomists,” insisting that faith in Christ had to be combined with law obedience in order to secure ultimate salvation”
- **locus:** L2581
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-013
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, justification]
- **claim:** Moo’s anti-pure-NPP stance: salvation history is crucial, but a deeper anthropological critique of “works” as human accomplishment underlies Galatians (esp. 3:10–12), hinted in 2:16 by Paul’s change of Ps 143:2’s “living one” to “flesh.”
- **quote:** “Yet implicit in Paul’s argument in Galatians and rising to the surface at several points is a more fundamental critique of “works” in terms of human-oriented accomplishment.”
- **locus:** L2583
- **passage:** Gal 2:16; 3:10–12

### C-R2-014
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, justification, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** Moo holds that sola fide is a legitimate theological derivation from Gal 2:16’s antitheses; “law” must not so dominate “works of the law” as to erase anthropological argument, nor should the phrase be treated as only irreducibly concrete torah-boundary language.
- **quote:** “The traditional Reformation emphasis on justification sola fide, “by faith alone,” is a legitimate theological derivation from the antitheses of Gal. 2:16.”
- **locus:** L2585
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-015
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, pistis-christou, justification]
- **claim:** Moo prefers the objective genitive for πίστις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ (“faith in Jesus Christ”) over the subjective (“faithfulness of Christ”), against a growing scholarly and some translational (NET, CEB) trend.
- **quote:** “we think this interpretation is preferable because (1) it matches Paul’s invariable custom of using the cognate verb to refer to human believing”
- **locus:** L2589
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-016
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, pistis-christou, abraham]
- **claim:** Contextual supports for the objective genitive at 2:16: the programmatic πίστις–justification link is resumed via Abraham’s believing (3:6); and εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν must be roughly equivalent to πίστις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ as basis for the central claim.
- **quote:** “εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν … must be roughly equivalent to πίστις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ”
- **locus:** L2589
- **passage:** Gal 2:16; 3:6

### C-R2-017
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** Against N. T. Wright’s covenantal membership reading of δικαιόω in Gal 2, Moo argues for forensic declaration of justice before God; that bedrock makes circumcision, Peter’s withdrawal, and the agitators’ program wrong—nothing must be added to faith in Christ for legal standing.
- **quote:** “Justification, one’s legal standing before God, is fully secured by faith in Christ. Nothing should be added; nothing can be added; nothing must be added”
- **locus:** L2591
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-018
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** On the three tenses of δικαιόω in 2:16, Moo finds deliberate temporal vagueness with a principial focus on faith alone, while the future and rhetorical situation imply some future aspect of justification against agitators who tied last-judgment verdict to works of the law.
- **quote:** “Paul responds that justification is always, whatever its time, a matter of faith and not works of the law—or of works of any kind.”
- **locus:** L2593
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-019
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, pistis-christou, justification]
- **claim:** Moo takes πιστεύω εἰς Χριστόν as directional faith toward Christ—trust and commitment beyond mere intellectual assent—and rejects Dunn’s reading of ἐὰν μή as allowing works-plus-faith exception in 2:16a.
- **quote:** “Pisteuo (or pistis) eis Christon depicts the committal of one’s self to the person of Christ, something more than an intellectual acceptance”
- **locus:** L2597
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-020
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Of two main options for 2:17–18, Moo prefers the postconversion reading: abandoning the law for justification “in Christ” makes Jewish Christians appear as Gentile-like “sinners,” yet only rebuilding the law as authority would truly make them transgressors.
- **quote:** “Neither interpretation is without its problems … but the second reading has fewer problems.”
- **locus:** L2613
- **passage:** Gal 2:17–18

### C-R2-021
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Justification “in Christ” (2:17) is local union with Christ; Moo argues this shows that 2:19–20’s union language is not a competing soteriological register but continuous with forensic justification.
- **quote:** “Justification takes place as believers are incorporated into Christ, and by sounding this note here, Paul reveals that the explicit teaching about this union with Christ in verses 19–20 is by no means a shift to a different, or competing, perspective”
- **locus:** L2615
- **passage:** Gal 2:17–20

### C-R2-022
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** On 2:18, “destroy/rebuild” refers to the law (esp. segregating provisions in light of Antioch): reinstituting the law as absolute authority brands the representative “I” a παραβάτης of that law—not Christ as servant of sin.
- **quote:** “if Peter, as a Jewish Christian, should try to reinstitute the law as an absolute authority for conduct … then he would, in effect, be rebuilding that which, in coming to Christ alone for justification, he had earlier torn down”
- **locus:** L2623
- **passage:** Gal 2:18

### C-R2-023
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** For 2:19–20, “died to the law” means release from Moses’ binding authority via radical death/new life with Christ; Moo slightly prefers “through the law” as frustration/failure under the law (cf. possible link to 3:10) over identification with Christ cursed by the law (3:13), though both are viable.
- **quote:** “But the former, in our view, makes slightly better sense of the passage and might find a parallel idea in Gal. 3:10”
- **locus:** L2633
- **passage:** Gal 2:19; 3:10, 13

### C-R2-024
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** “Crucified with Christ” is real identification with Christ’s cross (not mere metaphor of similar suffering); the old “I” under sin/law is done away with, and present life “in the flesh” is lived by faith in the Son of God (objective genitive again), who loved and gave himself for “me.”
- **quote:** “believers are regarded by God as having hung on the cross with Christ”
- **locus:** L2639
- **passage:** Gal 2:19–20

### C-R2-025
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** Moo rejects equating co-crucifixion with justification (Gorman et al.): proximity of 2:16–17 and 2:19–20 is not identity; 2:21 picks up righteousness/law from v. 16, not describing justification as co-crucifixion.
- **quote:** “this argument confuses proximity with identity. … There is no reason to suppose that they are describing justification.”
- **locus:** L2645
- **passage:** Gal 2:16–21

### C-R2-026
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** On 2:21, Moo takes “I do not set aside the grace of God” as Paul’s own final argument, not necessarily a rebuttal of an agitator accusation; connecting righteousness with the law introduces human-obedience qualification that makes Christ’s death of no effect.
- **quote:** “if we do not renounce all other hopes, and embrace Christ alone, we reject the grace of God.”
- **locus:** L2647
- **passage:** Gal 2:21

### C-R2-027
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, covenantal-nomism]
- **claim:** In the additional note on ἔργα νόμου, Moo concludes the phrase simply means things done in obedience to Moses’ law; NPP boundary-marker emphasis is inadequate; the ultimate reason the law is outmoded includes human captivity to sin, so “works of the law” can function as synecdoche for “works” generally.
- **quote:** “the Reformers, we think, were entirely justified in viewing Paul’s phrase “the works of the law” as a synecdoche for the more general category “works.””
- **locus:** L2667
- **passage:** Gal 2:16; Rom 3:20–28 context

### C-R2-028
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, new-perspective-on-paul]
- **claim:** Against Dunn’s claim that 4QMMT’s “works of the law” supports a boundary-marker reading, Moo judges the Qumran parallel unclear and the few Jewish precedents as denoting simply things done in obedience to the law.
- **quote:** “the Jewish precedents for Paul’s “works of the law” do not provide evidence that the phrase in itself functioned to signal the “boundary markers” connotation”
- **locus:** L2663
- **passage:** Gal 2:16

### C-R2-029
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, circumcision]
- **claim:** Even in Antioch-focused 2:16, Moo denies that works of the law are abandoned merely because they exclude Gentiles; the issue is what is necessary to complete salvation and avoid the curse (cf. 3:10–12; 5:2–6).
- **quote:** “the agitators … were insisting on works of the law not to maintain Israel’s special status … but to enable Gentile converts to “stay in” the realm of God’s grace”
- **locus:** L2665
- **passage:** Gal 2:16; 3:10–12; 5:2–6

### C-R2-030
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** Section III (3:1–5:12) defends the gospel of 2:15–21; the thread is works of the law vs. Christ-faith, finally as two means of accessing grace (doing vs. believing), not only a salvation-historical contrast of eras.
- **quote:** “the contrast between “works of the law” (or “law”) and “faith” is finally a contrast between two means of accessing God’s grace in Christ, between “doing the law” (or “doing”) and believing (in Christ).”
- **locus:** L2692
- **passage:** Gal 3:1–5:12; 2:16

### C-R2-031
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, abraham, justification]
- **claim:** Faith and Spirit serve dual ends: inclusion as Abraham’s/God’s children and justification/righteousness; Moo rejects Wright’s reduction of justification to recognition of belonging, treating justification as divine verdict granted to those who belong.
- **quote:** “It thus is better to view justification as God’s pronouncement of the righteous status that is granted to all who truly belong to the people of God.”
- **locus:** L2700
- **passage:** Gal 3:1–5:12

### C-R2-032
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, justification]
- **claim:** On 3:1–6, the rhetorical heart is not only how the Galatians began but how they continue: Spirit and blessings came by “hearing accompanied by faith,” not works of the law; Abraham’s Gen 15:6 experience corroborates faith’s importance and closes the paragraph for Moo.
- **quote:** ““hearing characterized by faith” is the means by which they will sustain their Christian experience (v. 3).”
- **locus:** L2722
- **passage:** Gal 3:1–6

### C-R2-033
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, galatians, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** “Foolish Galatians” signals intellectual failure; “bewitched” (βασκαίνω) is neither pure sorcery report nor mere rhetoric but suggests evil spiritual influence; the cross was “publicly portrayed” in Paul’s vivid preaching, which should rule out human-oriented law programs.
- **quote:** “When truly appreciated, the cross of Christ … should rule out of court the kind of human-oriented law program that the agitators are perpetrating.”
- **locus:** L2732
- **passage:** Gal 3:1

### C-R2-034
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, pistis-christou, works-of-the-law]
- **claim:** Reception of the Spirit marks the new age; Moo rejects reading ἀκοὴ πίστεως as “faith-message” or “message about Christ’s faithfulness,” tying πίστις to human believing confirmed by the Abraham link (3:6).
- **quote:** “making it likely that the reference here also is to human believing in Christ. And this interpretation receives confirmation from the connection that Paul makes between the Galatians’ πίστις and Abraham’s faith (v. 6)”
- **locus:** L2736
- **passage:** Gal 3:2, 5–6

### C-R2-035
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** Moo prefers ἀκοή as the activity of hearing (faithful receptivity including trust and disposition to obey), with πίστεως attributive/epexegetic—“hearing accompanied by faith” / hearing that is faith—reminding them of initial gospel response.
- **quote:** “so it is also possible that the phrase in this verse (and in v. 5) means “hearing accompanied by faith””
- **locus:** L2738
- **passage:** Gal 3:2, 5

### C-R2-036
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, works-of-the-law, circumcision, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** On 3:3, “by the flesh” may allude to circumcision but is broader Pauline “human effort/existence”; because works of the law are a subset of works, Paul’s warning targets synergism (faith + torah for sonship and ultimate righteousness), not the importance of Spirit-produced obedience.
- **quote:** “It is this synergism with respect to righteousness that Paul denies.”
- **locus:** L2742
- **passage:** Gal 3:3

### C-R2-037
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, galatians]
- **claim:** Moo prefers the usual NT sense “suffer” for ἐπάθετε in 3:4 (not “experience pleasant things”), linked to persecution contexts; εἴ γε καί εἰκῇ sounds a hopeful note that Paul cannot quite believe their experience was in vain.
- **quote:** “We think it is better, then, to keep the normal NT sense of πάσχω in this verse.”
- **locus:** L2746
- **passage:** Gal 3:4

### C-R2-038
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, justification]
- **claim:** Gen 15:6 is Abraham’s faith credited as righteousness—God graciously viewed faith as fulfilling what God expected for right standing (not yet covenant membership); Paul fairly applies it to forensic faith–righteousness for the Galatians.
- **quote:** “God graciously viewed Abraham’s faith as having in itself fulfilled all that God expected of Abraham in order for him to be in the right before God.”
- **locus:** L2760
- **passage:** Gal 3:6; Gen 15:6

### C-R2-039
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, holy-spirit, justification]
- **claim:** Spirit in 3:1–5 confirms entry into relationship with God, not that “righteousness” includes Spirit-transformation; righteousness is right standing at every stage through faith, against agitators’ views.
- **quote:** “the Spirit functions in verses 1–5 not as an agent of transformation but as the confirmation that the believers have indeed entered into relationship with God.”
- **locus:** L2762
- **passage:** Gal 3:1–6

### C-R2-040
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, justification, works-of-the-law]
- **claim:** In 3:7–4:7 Paul answers agitators’ Abraham rhetoric: (1) faith alone is adequate for righteous standing (developed in 3:10–12 against works/works of any kind); (2) salvation-historically, torah came after promise and was temporary until Messiah—hence not necessary to Abrahamic righteousness.
- **quote:** “In verses 10–12, Paul is at pains to show that “works of the law”—and by extension, “works” of any kind—add nothing to the adequacy of faith as a means of righteousness”
- **locus:** L2820
- **passage:** Gal 3:7–14

### C-R2-041
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** On 3:7, οἱ ἐκ πίστεως are those marked/characterized by (depending on) faith—human faith continuous with Abraham’s believing in v. 6, not primarily God’s or Christ’s faithfulness (against Howard, de Boer, Hays).
- **quote:** “verse 6 is certainly primary; and verse 6 refers unambiguously to the faith of Abraham.”
- **locus:** L2894
- **passage:** Gal 3:6–7

### C-R2-042
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, justification]
- **claim:** Scripture “announced the gospel ahead of time” to Abraham (Gen 12:3 conflated with parallel promises, esp. 18:18’s πάντα τὰ ἔθνη): justification by faith of Gentiles is foundational to gospel content, though not exhausting it.
- **quote:** “this verse shows that “justification by faith,” while not exhausting the meaning of “gospel,” is certainly foundational to it.”
- **locus:** L2902
- **passage:** Gal 3:8

### C-R2-043
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, justification]
- **claim:** Verse 9 concludes that those of faith are blessed with Abraham the “man of faith” (πιστός = believing, not merely faithful); blessing is closely associated (if not identified) with justification; inclusion of Gentiles is important but the more fundamental concern is faith as access for Jew and Gentile.
- **quote:** “his more fundamental concern … is to show that faith is the means by which Jews and Gentiles alike can access the blessing.”
- **locus:** L2908
- **passage:** Gal 3:9

### C-R2-044
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, justification, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** Moo reconstructs 3:10 as a traditional syllogism: only complete doers escape the curse (Deut 27:26); no one does all the law (assumed; cf. 5:3); therefore those who depend on works of the law are under a curse—preferring this over narratival Israel-exile/boundary-marker readings (Wright, Stanley, Scott et al.).
- **quote:** “No one who depends on doing the law will escape the curse (v. 10a).”
- **locus:** L2918–L2924
- **passage:** Gal 3:10; Deut 27:26

### C-R2-045
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy, justification]
- **claim:** Critical to Moo’s logic: “works of the law” and “doing” at the end of the quotation are the same thing; Paul moves from “doing tied to outmoded law” to the deeper issue that the law involves impossible human “doing.”
- **quote:** “the law provides no basis for the blessing because it involves ‘doing’: a ‘doing’ that humans find to be impossible.”
- **locus:** L2930
- **passage:** Gal 3:10

### C-R2-046
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** Moo answers the “unfulfillability not assumed in Judaism” objection: Deuteronomy’s “all,” Gal 5:3’s “whole law,” and post-cross either-or (Christ as sole atonement) require perfect obedience if law-doing is to furnish blessing.
- **quote:** “This new “either-or” situation created by the climax of salvation history now forces obedience to the law to be perfect if it is to furnish a basis for the blessing”
- **locus:** L2932
- **passage:** Gal 3:10; 5:3

### C-R2-047
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** On 3:11 syntax, Moo retains traditional logic: it is clear no one is justified by the law *because* Hab 2:4 privileges faith; he rejects reversing the clauses (Wakefield, CEB, Hays et al.) as poorer logic and pattern of scriptural grounding.
- **quote:** “The OT claim that people are justified by faith (11b) constitutes logical grounds for the negative claim that people are not justified in the law.”
- **locus:** L2934
- **passage:** Gal 3:11; Hab 2:4

### C-R2-048
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** In Hab 2:4 as Paul cites it, πίστις is human faith (not Christ’s); “live” is soteriological; Moo slightly prefers construing ἐκ πίστεως with ζήσεται (“will live by faith”), a legitimate “deepening” of Habakkuk’s call to firm trust.
- **quote:** “Paul’s application of Hab. 2:4 is just that: a legitimate reappropriation of a key prophetic witness to the priority of faith in relating to God.”
- **locus:** L2940
- **passage:** Gal 3:11; Hab 2:4

### C-R2-049
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, works-of-the-law, justification, new-perspective-on-paul-controversy]
- **claim:** Verse 12: the law is not “of faith” (not “based on faith” as origin) but stands outside the ἐκ πίστεως sphere of Hab 2:4; Lev 18:5 sets “doing” as the law’s path to life, antithetically parallel to living by faith—so dependence on doing yields curse, not life.
- **quote:** “The Reformers, therefore, were entirely justified to find in Paul’s argument here a fundamental and universally valid principle about the exclusive value of believing versus doing.”
- **locus:** L2952
- **passage:** Gal 3:11–12; Lev 18:5; Hab 2:4

### C-R2-050
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** On the “us” of 3:13–14, Moo slightly prefers the inclusive Christian reading over Jewish-Christians-only: Christ redeems Jew and Gentile from the curse standing over all who fail God’s demands (clearest in Mosaic law), warning Galatians against law-dependence (v. 10).
- **quote:** “Paul assures them in verse 13 that they have themselves been definitively rescued … from the curse that stands over all human beings by virtue of their failure to meet the demands of God”
- **locus:** L3148
- **passage:** Gal 3:13–14

### C-R2-051
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Christ redeems by becoming a curse “for us” (ὑπέρ with substitutionary identification); Deut 21:23 (as applied to crucifixion in contemporary Judaism) illustrates that the hung one is cursed—Christ for others’ sins, paralleling 2 Cor 5:21.
- **quote:** “Christ suffered exclusion from the people of God and, more terribly, separation from God the Father himself (Mark 15:34), so that those people who had been excluded because of their sin could be brought back in again.”
- **locus:** L3152
- **passage:** Gal 3:13; Deut 21:23

### C-R2-052
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, holy-spirit, justification, pistis-christou]
- **claim:** Two coordinate purpose/result clauses in 3:14: Abraham’s blessing (justification) comes to Gentiles *in* Christ Jesus (locative, not by law/Israel identification), and “we” receive the promise of the Spirit through (human) faith—related but not identical new-covenant gifts, closing the inclusio with 3:1–5.
- **quote:** “Gentiles experience the blessing of Abraham not by identification with Israel through the law but simply and definitively by their relationship to Christ Jesus.”
- **locus:** L3158
- **passage:** Gal 3:14

## Coverage summary

- **2:15–21 structure and function:** Transitional definition of gospel truth (C-001–005); forensic vs. participatory debate (C-006–007); Antioch continuity and v. 16 thesis (C-008–009).
- **Works of the law / NPP:** Denotation (C-010); NPP covenantal-nomism summary granted in part (C-011–012); Moo’s anthropological deepening and synecdoche-for-works (C-013–014, C-027–029); agitators as nomists, stay-in/curse concerns.
- **Pistis Christou:** Objective genitive preferred with grammatical/contextual arguments (C-015–016, C-019, C-024); Hab/Abraham links reinforce human faith; Hays narrative “faith of Christ” reading rejected in additional note material summarized via C-041 and section framing.
- **Justification:** Forensic standing (C-017–018); not membership reduction (C-017, C-031); not co-crucifixion (C-025); grace vs. law-righteousness (C-026).
- **2:17–21:** Postconversion “sinners” reading (C-020–022); died to law / crucified with Christ (C-023–024); v. 21 grace (C-026).
- **3:1–6:** Spirit by hearing of faith; foolishness/bewitching/cross placard; flesh as human effort; suffer; Gen 15:6 (C-032–039).
- **3:7–14:** Sons of Abraham by faith; gospel-to-Abraham; blessing = faith access (C-040–043); Deut 27:26 syllogism vs. exile-narrative NPP (C-044–046); Hab 2:4 and Lev 18:5 believing-vs-doing (C-047–049); Christ-curse redemption inclusive; blessing in Christ + Spirit by faith (C-050–052).
- **Not present in range beyond scaffolding:** Full 3:15–4:7 promise/law sequence is introduced in section intros but not fully exposited in this slice’s exclusive body (ends at 3:14 notes).
